note: A reusable methodological device first named in S0363: if removing a candidate Kernel responsibility X breaks no invariant, X is not Kernel responsibility. May be a distinct methodological object or may simply remain folded into the general Kernel-discovery discussion; not confirmed as independently named in later batches.
A five-role decomposition of lifecycle-transition responsibility (who detects/proposes/adjudicates/applies/records) introduced in S0364 to prevent conflating them under one Kernel/aggregate owner.

The classical Nyaya four-part epistemology (claim/means-of-knowledge/valid-cognition/knower) applied as an architectural lens in S0365 and S0369, distinct from the relational Navya-Nyaya lens; may already exist under a broader 'Nyaya/Tarka' label not covered by this batch's read.

The Navya-Nyaya lens treating relations (svarupa-sambandha, etc.) as first-class rather than object properties, applied repeatedly across S0365, S0367, S0368, S0392 to challenge whether Evidence/Justification/state belong inside an aggregate as properties or as relations.
A structural (not literal-theological) lens distinguishing what remains invariant (Shiva) from what legitimately transforms (Shakti), introduced in S0366 and reused in S0367, S0370-S0372, S0383.

A mathematical lens (connectedness, boundaries, neighborhoods, continuity under deformation) proposed in S0384 as distinct from Escher, with a five-item failure-mode taxonomy; the source file itself explicitly declines to claim admission into the formal lens register, classifying it only as a strongly-justified analytical lens pending governance decision.

Ten candidate East-Asian epistemic lenses proposed in S0393, ranked for Kernel-finding usefulness in S0394, and applied at length (alongside Daoism/Confucianism/Mohism/Xunzi/Zhuangzi/Yin-Yang/Huayan/Zhu-Xi) in the large multi-agent research commission S0397; explicitly treated as temporary cross-validation instruments, never proposed for formal admission to the 26-lens register.

A nine-principle lens (W1-W9) extracted from Timothy Williamson's 'Knowledge and its Limits' in S0399, covering factive knowledge, E=K, temporal defeasibility, margin-for-error/robustness, anti-luminosity, non-iteration of higher-order knowledge, structural unknowability, and assertion-as-authority-boundary; explicitly kept separate from the Tarka 'Argument Falsification Lens' (S0398).

A ten-point falsification checklist (T1-T10) derived directly from the classical Nyaya logic textbook Tarka-sangraha/Dipika in S0398 (lakshana definition-defects, five-member inference, vyapti/anvaya/vyatireka, hetvabhasa fallacies, samsaya, viparyaya, abhava/pratiyogi, nigrahasthana), explicitly scoped as an argument-validity lens distinct from the Williamson epistemic-status lens.

A ten-principle model (A1-A10) extracted from Robert Audi's epistemology in S0402, centered on distinguishing causal/justificational/epistemic grounding and warning that AI-generated same-source claim chains are not independent corroboration ('artificial coherence'); combined with the Williamson lens into a composite KnowledgeOS Epistemic Model.

Proposed in S0367 as possibly the more fundamental root domain object than Kernel/Knowledge/KnowledgeAggregate -- the domain object whose integrity KnowledgeOS actually protects -- with two competing candidate shapes sketched but left unresolved.

A named element (disagreement preservation, supersession tracking, resolution history) proposed as co-equal with KnowledgeAggregate and Lifecycle inside the Kernel boundary, first appearing concretely in S0393 and carried into the ADR-KOS-KERNEL-001 draft (S0395) as its own separate consistency boundary/aggregate, explicitly not merged with KnowledgeAggregate.
